subject: health
essentialQuestion: What has to keep happening when no one reminds me?

prompts.prompt: Explain building routines that survive a schedule change in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of sleep, movement, fueling, and recovery as maintained systems rather than goals.
Apply tracking what matters without measuring the body in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving managing a routine through illness, stress, or a heavy period; correct it and explain why.
Connect restarting after a routine collapses, without self-punishment with deciding what to keep, drop, and add each season. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build an independent maintenance system with a normal-week version, a hard-week fallback version, and a written restart procedure. Progress is described in terms of behaviors kept, never body measurements.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: The system may be written, tabled, built as a checklist, entered in a calendar, or described aloud to an adult. Any component the learner cannot perform is planned as a supported or adapted component and scored equally.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
trustedAdultNote: Direct any urgent safety, health, or mental-health concern to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
